title: Vermont Statutes Annotated, Title 21 (Labor), Chapter 5 (Employment Practices), Subchapter 4A - Parental and Family Leave
verified_how: fetched https://legislature.vermont.gov/statutes/chapter/21/005 (HTTP 200): headings 'Title 21 : Labor' and 'Chapter 005 : Employment Practices', subchapter heading 'Subchapter 004A : PARENTAL AND FAMILY LEAVE' listing s 470 (Purpose), 471 (Definitions), 472 (Leave), 472a (Short-term family leave), 472b (Town meeting leave; employees; students), 472c (Leave; alleged crime victims; relief from stalking or abuse), 473 (Retaliation prohibited) and 474 (Penalties and enforcement), none marked repealed. Every page of the Vermont Statutes Online carries the currency line 'The Statutes below include the actions of the 2025 session of the General Assembly.' and the caveat 'NOTE: The Vermont Statutes Online is an unofficial copy of the Vermont Statutes Annotated that is provided as a convenience.' No repeal marker appears on the cited provisions; repealed sections elsewhere in the same chapters are explicitly flagged 'Repealed. <act cite>', so the absence of that marker is meaningful.
notes: Vermont's paid sick time mandate is the neighbouring Subchapter 4B, EARNED SICK TIME (21 V.S.A. ss 481-487), verified in force on the same page. There is no Vermont statute requiring paid public holidays or paid vacation for private-sector employees.
